extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their legal/financial reporting/compliance teams (and their advisers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements for public-company climate-related disclosures under the SEC's Item 1500/1502 regime, including transition plans, scenario analysis, internal carbon pricing, and board oversight disclosures. Intended to direct what must be disclosed, when (materiality), and how much detail to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan disclosure — material expenditures and material impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding to Item 1502(e), a registrant must disclose material expenditures or material impacts on its financial estimates and assumptions that directly resulted from actions taken under the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants have flexibility to explain qualitatively the nature of a material expenditure or material impact and how it directly resulted from actions taken under the plan. When individual expenditures are immaterial, registrants should consider whether overall expenditures related to actions taken under the plan are material in the aggregate and, if so, provide appropriate disclosure (e.g., a series of individually immaterial expenditures could be material in the aggregate). To the extent such information is disclosed in response to Rule 14-02(h) of Regulation S-X, cross-referencing is permitted. Compliance with tracking/reporting provisions (Item 1502(e)(2)) is phased in: a registrant is not required to comply until the fiscal year immediately following the fiscal year of its initial compliance date for the subpart 1500 rules based on filer status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan disclosure required only when plan adopted to manage a material transition risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The transition plan disclosure provision requires disclosure only when a plan has been adopted to manage a material transition risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focusing the requirement on adopted plans for material transition risks helps mitigate concerns about disclosure of confidential or proprietary information and reduces the risk that the rule would disincentivize adoption of transition plans. The rule does not require board approval as the determinative factor for disclosure; plans adopted by senior management that materially affect financial condition or operations may require disclosure even if not board-approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical risks excluded from transition plan disclosure (but disclosed elsewhere if material)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference to physical risks was removed from the transition plan disclosure requirement; transition-plan disclosure focuses on transition risks. A registrant that faces a material physical risk is still required to disclose how it is managing that risk as part of its risk management disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns transition plan disclosure more closely with voluntary TCFD-based disclosures and reduces complexity for registrants familiar with that framework. Physical risks should be disclosed under the separate risk management disclosure provisions when material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate-related opportunities disclosure is optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure regarding climate-related opportunities included in a transition plan is optional; the final rule treats disclosure of opportunities as optional and does not require registrants to disclose how they intend to achieve any climate-related opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treating opportunity disclosure as optional addresses anti-competitive concerns and avoids requiring disclosure of plans that could reveal proprietary strategies. Registrants may elect to describe opportunities or how they intend to achieve them, but are not required to do so under Item 1502.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis disclosure — when used and material
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant uses scenario analysis to assess the impact of climate-related risks on its business, results of operations, or financial condition, and based on the results determines that a climate-related risk is reasonably likely to have a material impact, then the registrant must describe each such scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required description must include a brief description of the parameters, assumptions, and analytical choices used, as well as the expected material impacts, including financial impacts, on the registrant under each scenario. The rule is limited to scenario analysis (the term 'any analytical tools' was removed) and does not require any registrant to conduct scenario analysis. The disclosure requirement was streamlined: the term 'brief' was added to limit detail; the prior example temperature scenarios were removed to avoid implying required scenarios; the prior requirement to include both qualitative and quantitative information was removed to allow registrants to provide the mix that fits their circumstances. The disclosure is subject to a materiality qualifier and safe harbor (see related entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis — materiality qualifier and safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenario analysis disclosure is required only if the registrant's use of scenario analysis leads it to determine that a climate-related risk is reasonably likely to have a material impact on the business, results of operations, or financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This materiality qualifier was added to address concerns about burdensome or immaterial disclosures. Scenario analysis disclosure will be subject to a safe harbor. The Commission also streamlined requirements to avoid redundancy (e.g., eliminated a separate requirement to describe 'resilience of strategy' since that is encompassed by scenario disclosure when used). Registrants may select the climate scenario model(s) they believe best fit their industry or business; the rules do not prescribe specific models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal carbon price disclosure — when use is material
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that uses internal carbon pricing must disclose certain information about the internal carbon price only when such use is material to how it evaluates and manages a climate-related risk identified in response to Item 1502(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material, the registrant must disclose in units of the registrant's reporting currency: (1) the price per metric ton of CO2e; and (2) the total price, including how the total price is estimated to change over the time periods referenced in Item 1502(a), as applicable. If a registrant uses more than one internal carbon price to evaluate/manage a material climate-related risk, it must provide the required disclosures for each internal carbon price and disclose its reasons for using different prices. If the scope of entities/operations included in the internal carbon price is materially different from the organizational boundaries used for GHG emissions measurement, the registrant must briefly describe this difference. The final rule eliminated the proposed requirements to separately describe how the registrant uses the internal carbon price and the rationale for selecting the price, to reduce burden and protect potentially confidential/proprietary information. Internal carbon price disclosure is subject to a safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — identify board members or board committees with oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must identify any board members or board committees responsible for the oversight of climate-related risks, whether an existing committee (e.g., audit or risk committee) or a separate committee established for climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of the responsible board member(s) or committee(s) is intended to provide investors transparency into who at the board level oversees climate-related risks. This aligns with the TCFD framework and is not intended to prescribe particular board structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — disclose board members' climate-related expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose whether any member of the board of directors possesses expertise in climate-related risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This detailed disclosure about board expertise is intended to inform investors about the qualifications of board members with respect to climate-related risk oversight. The proposal sought detailed disclosure but did not require or encourage any particular board composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — describe processes and frequency of board discussions on climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe the processes and frequency by which the board or board committee discusses climate-related risks, including how the board is informed about such risks and how frequently the board considers them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure should explain how the board receives information on climate risks and how often climate risks are considered, to help investors assess the degree to which board oversight is integrated into corporate governance and strategic planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — disclose how board considers climate-related risks in strategy, risk management, and financial oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose whether and how the board or board committee considered climate-related risks as part of its business strategy, risk management, and financial oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is intended to give investors information regarding how the board considers climate-related risks when reviewing and guiding business strategy and major plans of action; setting and monitoring risk management policies and performance objectives; reviewing/approving annual budgets; and overseeing major expenditures, acquisitions, and divestitures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — disclose whether/how the board sets climate-related targets or goals and evaluates progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose whether and how the board sets climate-related targets or goals and how it evaluates progress, including the establishment of any interim targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information helps investors evaluate whether and how a board is preparing to mitigate or adapt to material transition risks. If applicable, a registrant may also describe the board's oversight of climate-related opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance — optional disclosure of board oversight of climate-related opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may describe the board of directors' oversight of climate-related opportunities (this disclosure is optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed goal was to elicit decision-useful information about board oversight without encouraging particular board practices or affecting how a registrant operates. Opportunity-related disclosures remain permissive.
